draft.title: Business goals
card: A goal is something a business sets out to achieve. Goals give the owners and workers a clear target to work towards.
Profit
Earning more from sales than the business spends on costs. Growth means getting bigger, such as selling more or opening new shops.
Market share
The part of all sales in a market that one business wins. Customer service means looking after customers well so that they come back.
Sustainability
Running the business in a way that looks after the environment and community, so it can carry on over the long term.
draft.remember: A business can set several goals at once, such as profit, growth, market share, service and sustainability.

a.q: Mia's bakery in Bendigo wants to sell more bread than the other bakeries in town. Which goal is this?
opts: Winning a bigger share of the market
a.why: Selling more than rival bakeries means taking a bigger part of the town's bread sales, which is market share. Profit is about earning more than costs, not about beating rivals on sales.
a.clue: Think about how much of the town's bread sales she wants.

b.q: Omar's cycle shop in Geelong switches to recycled packaging and repairs old bikes instead of throwing them out. Which goal is he mainly pursuing?
b.why: Recycled packaging and repairing old bikes look after the environment, so this is sustainability. It may also please customers, but the actions are aimed at protecting the environment, not at service.
b.clue: Which goal is about looking after the environment?

a.best: Winning a bigger share of the market

problems.detail: The right option, 'Winning a bigger share of the market', is clearly the longest (six words against two or three for the others), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
The clue 'Which goal is about looking after the environment?' gives the answer away. Only one option is about the environment, so the student just matches words and does not have to apply the idea.

proposal.title: Business goals
card: A goal is something a business sets out to achieve. Goals give owners and workers a clear target, and a business can have several at once.
Making a profit means earning more from sales than the business spends on costs. Growth means getting bigger, such as selling more or opening new shops.
Market share is the part of all sales in a market that one business wins. Serving customers well means looking after them so they come back.
Acting sustainably means running the business in a way that looks after the environment and community, so it can carry on over the long term.
proposal.remember: Common business goals are profit, growth, market share, serving customers well and acting sustainably.

a.q: Mia's bakery in Bendigo wants more of the town's bread buyers to choose her shop instead of rival bakeries. Which goal is this?
a.why: Taking buyers from rival bakeries means winning a bigger part of the town's bread sales, which is market share. Profit is about earning more than the business spends on costs, not about beating rivals for buyers.
a.clue: Her aim is about her rivals, not her costs.

b.q: Omar's cycle shop in Geelong switches to recycled packaging and fixes old bikes so fewer end up in landfill. Which goal is he mainly pursuing?
b.why: Recycling and keeping bikes out of landfill look after the environment, so this is sustainability. Some customers may like it, but the actions are aimed at cutting waste, not at looking after customers.
b.clue: Ask what cutting waste protects over the long term.
